issue: Register wobble: 'aku' is the only non-saya first-person pronoun in nodes 33-34 (all sibling anecdote cards use saya; aku is otherwise clustered in the later intimate-register block from id-3180 on). Mixing 'aku' with formal conjunction 'tetapi' in the same clause is also incongruous.

fix.target: Ceritanya saya mau berhemat bulan ini, tetapi ada diskon besar di mana-mana.

issue: Gloss garbled: 'what happened isn't necessarily true' asserts the event occurred and questions its truth, which is backwards — 'belum tentu benar kejadiannya' means it is not certain the thing actually happened at all. Target sentence itself is natural.

fix.english: All that is just what people say; it's not necessarily what really happened.

issue: Gloss tense clash: 'before we knew it, he has now become famous' mixes past 'knew' with present perfect + 'now' — unnatural English that will read as a translation error. Target sentence is a good tahu-tahu use.

fix.english: He used to come to this food stall often; before we knew it, he'd become a famous person.

issue: Sequencing: 'cuma' makes its deck-wide debut here (node-33), 91 cards before its register tip at id-2951 where the hanya/cuma contrast is actually taught. An untipped colloquialism debut violates the heard-vs-modeled discipline the slice otherwise keeps; hanya preserves the sentence and defers cuma to its tipped card.

fix.target: Katanya dia hanya mau melihat-lihat, ujung-ujungnya dia pulang membawa tiga kantong belanja.

issue: 'Sudah diberi jalan lebih dekat' misfires: 'diberi jalan' is the fixed expression 'given way / let through', so the clause reads 'having been yielded to closer' — an English calque of 'given a shorter route'. Indonesian shows someone a route (ditunjukkan jalan), it doesn't give one.

fix.target: Sudah ditunjukkan jalan yang lebih dekat, dia malah memilih jalan memutar.
fix.english: He'd already been shown a shorter route; instead he chose the long way around.

issue: Dangling connective: the card opens with 'Sampai-sampai' but sampai-sampai is a consequence clause that needs an antecedent in the same sentence; as a standalone SRS card it is a fragment ('So much so that...' with no 'so much' stated). Restructure to carry its own cause.

fix.target: Kami tertawa terlalu keras, sampai-sampai tetangga ikut keluar.
fix.english: We laughed too loudly, so much so that the neighbors came out too.

issue: 'salah memakai kacamata orang lain' double-marks the mistake and comes out wrong: salah memakai = put on the WRONG one, so adding 'orang lain' yields 'wrongly wore someone else's glasses'. Natural phrasing is either 'salah memakai kacamata' or 'tidak sengaja memakai kacamata orang lain'.

fix.target: Dia menahan tawa waktu bos tidak sengaja memakai kacamata orang lain.
fix.english: He held back laughter when the boss accidentally put on someone else's glasses.

issue: Heard-particle policy breach: 'sih' is modeled in the learner's own first-person voice, while the sibling particles lho (id-2891) and kok (id-2892) are correctly quarantined inside quoted speech. Policy rule 3: heard language, not modeled language. Quote it and make the tip say recognize-don't-copy, matching the lho card.

fix.target: Teman saya bilang, "Filmnya bagus sih, cuma terlalu panjang."
fix.english: My friend said, "The movie's good, I admit — it's just too long."
fix.grammar: Sih = spoken particle you'll hear everywhere: bagus sih = it's good, I admit. Recognize it — no need to use it.

issue: Formal boilerplate slightly wrong: real surat keterangan certificates close with 'untuk dipergunakan sebagaimana mestinya' (or digunakan) — 'dipakai' is too casual for this fixed formula, and the whole point of the card is the authentic wording.

fix.target: Surat keterangan kerja ini dibuat untuk dipergunakan sebagaimana mestinya.
fix.english: This employment certificate is issued to be used as appropriate.

newTokens.dipergunakan: be used (formal certificate boilerplate, from guna)

issue: Formal sign card lacks a register-naming tip: the tip is pure morphology (peN-) and never tells the learner this is sign language or what people actually say. Policy rule 4 requires formal cards to name the register.

fix.target: Area ini khusus untuk pemegang kartu anggota.
fix.english: This area is exclusively for membership card holders.
fix.grammar: Sign word: pemegang kartu = 'card holder' (peN- = the holder) — spoken: yang punya kartu anggota.

issue: Inaccurate everyday-equivalent in tip: 'speech often servis' is misleading here — servis means repair/maintenance service (servis motor); for layanan pelanggan people say CS, never 'servis pelanggan'. The tip risks teaching a wrong collocation.

fix.target: Layanan pelanggan kami dapat dihubungi dua puluh empat jam.
fix.english: Our customer service can be reached twenty-four hours a day.
fix.grammar: layanan = formal 'service', from melayani — in speech, customer service is just CS (ce-es).

issue: The formal Indonesian is off: bank notices say 'penarikan (tunai)' for withdrawals and ask customers to 'konfirmasi/dikonfirmasi sehari sebelumnya' — 'pengambilan uang ... harap dilaporkan' (be reported) is not how any bank phrases it. Tip repeats the wrong noun.

fix.target: Penarikan uang di atas sepuluh juta harap dikonfirmasi sehari sebelumnya.
fix.english: Withdrawals above ten million should be confirmed one day in advance.
fix.grammar: penarikan uang = 'withdrawal', bank language — spoken: mau ambil uang.

issue: Gloss overtranslates: pahit banget = 'really bitter', not 'way too bitter' — 'too' would be terlalu/kepahitan. The card teaches banget = sekali/sangat, so the gloss should not smuggle in excess.

fix.target: Kopi di kedai baru itu pahit banget menurutku.
fix.english: The coffee at that new cafe is really bitter, if you ask me.

issue: Internal register clash: 'akhir pekan' is flagged by this deck's own tip (id-3132) as the news word — 'in conversation everyone says weekend or Sabtu-Minggu' — yet here it sits in a slang card next to 'lagi ngapain'. Recast with the conversational form.

fix.target: Dia tanya aku lagi ngapain Sabtu-Minggu ini.
fix.english: She asked what I was up to this weekend.

issue: Incoherent register mix: nobody who softens with dong asks 'seru tidak?' — the natural tag with dong is 'seru nggak?'. nggak is already sanctioned in this node (id-3176ff), so the fix stays within taught material.

fix.target: Cerita dong, liburanmu di Bali kemarin seru nggak?
fix.english: Come on, tell me — was your Bali trip fun or not?

issue: Colloquial card missing its register tip: this is the first (and only) occurrence of the interjection 'duh' in the slice and the card has no grammar tip at all — policy rule 3 requires sanctioned colloquials to carry a tip.

fix.target: Duh, aku ketinggalan dompet di rumah lagi.
fix.english: Ugh, I left my wallet at home again.
fix.grammar: Duh = 'ugh/oh no', the spoken groan for small disasters: duh, ketinggalan dompet!

issue: Internal register clash: the deck's own tip (id-3112) says 'in real life everyone says HP', yet this everyday-speech card (a parent nagging a child) uses written-register 'ponsel'. In node-36 the spoken word belongs in the sentence.

fix.target: Jangan main HP terus, matamu bisa sakit.
fix.english: Stop playing on your phone all the time — your eyes will hurt.
fix.grammar: Main HP = 'be on your phone' — HP (ha-pe) is what everyone calls a phone in speech.

issue: Process error: the stated order (akta kelahiran first, THEN name enters KK) is backwards. Adding a newborn to the KK needs the hospital's surat keterangan lahir, not the akta; under Dukcapil's integrated service the akta, updated KK, and KIA are issued together in one visit. The card teaches a wrong bureaucratic sequence in the node whose whole point is sequence accuracy.

fix.target: Nama anak dimasukkan ke kartu keluarga bersamaan dengan pengurusan akta kelahirannya.
fix.english: The child's name is added to the family card at the same time as the birth certificate is processed.
fix.grammar: Bersamaan dengan = at the same time as: diurus bersamaan = processed together — one Dukcapil visit.

issue: Currency: the kelas 1-2-3 room system is being phased out — Perpres 59/2024 mandated the standard inpatient class (KRIS) in place of class-based rooms from mid-2025, so 'kelas rawat menentukan kamar' is stale-to-wrong for a 2026 learner walking into a hospital.

fix.target: Kamar pasien BPJS sekarang mulai disamakan lewat kelas rawat inap standar.
fix.english: BPJS patient rooms are now starting to be standardized through the standard inpatient class.
fix.grammar: KRIS (kelas rawat inap standar) is replacing the old kelas 1–3 — one standard room class for all.

issue: Stale terminology: from the 2025/2026 intake, PPDB was rebranded SPMB and 'jalur zonasi' was renamed 'jalur domisili' (placement by home address). Parents still say zonasi colloquially, but a card teaching the official track name should teach the current one.

fix.target: Kami mendaftarkan anak ke sekolah dekat rumah lewat jalur domisili.
fix.english: We registered our child at a school near home through the residence track.
fix.grammar: Jalur domisili = placement by home address — the 2025 rename of the old jalur zonasi.

issue: Logic/custom error: Imlek is a one-day national holiday — falling on a Monday cannot by itself close an office for two days. The real two-day closure comes from cuti bersama (a government joint-leave day) attached to the holiday; the card misses the chance to teach that essential calendar word.

fix.target: Kantor teman saya libur dua hari karena ada cuti bersama setelah hari raya Imlek.
fix.english: My friend's office is off for two days because there is a joint leave day after Imlek.
fix.grammar: Cuti bersama = government-set joint leave glued onto holidays — Indonesia's long-weekend maker.

issue: Gloss infidelity: in English you fill a PRESCRIPTION, not a medicine — 'this medicine has to be filled' is broken pharmacy English. 'Ditebus' = redeemed/bought against the prescription. The tip repeats the same 'filled' error.

fix.target: Obat ini harus ditebus dengan resep dokter di apotek.
fix.english: You can only get this medicine with a doctor's prescription at the pharmacy.
fix.grammar: Obat resep = prescription medicine: ditebus dengan resep = bought only against a prescription.

issue: Tip defect: final sentence 'The -kan asks it done' is garbled English and explains nothing about causative -kan. Sentence itself is fine.

fix.target: Kalau demamnya tidak turun dalam tiga hari, segera periksakan ke dokter.
fix.english: If the fever doesn't go down in three days, have it checked by a doctor right away.
fix.grammar: Periksakan = have it checked: periksakan ke dokter = get a doctor to look at it.

issue: Factual usage error: Indonesians read phone and emergency numbers digit by digit — 112 is 'satu satu dua', never 'seratus dua belas'. The card actively teaches a reading no one would use when calling for help.

fix.target: Nomor darurat di Indonesia adalah satu satu dua, mudah diingat.
fix.english: The emergency number in Indonesia is one-one-two, easy to remember.
fix.grammar: Numbers you dial are read digit by digit: 112 = satu satu dua, never seratus dua belas.

issue: Dangling clause after 'bilang': 'orang Indonesia bilang sedang masuk angin' never names who is masuk angin, so the report has no subject. Natural speech supplies it: 'bilang kamu sedang masuk angin'.

fix.target: Kalau badan pegal dan meriang, orang Indonesia bilang kamu sedang masuk angin.
fix.english: When your body is achy and feverish, Indonesians say you have 'masuk angin'.
fix.grammar: Masuk angin ('wind got in') = the classic catch-all unwellness: chills, bloating, fatigue. Untranslatable.

issue: 'Meskipun modern' is a dangling English-style adjective — a person isn't 'modern' the way a building is; the concessive clause reads translated. The doctor-tolerates-kerokan framing itself is good and worth keeping.

fix.target: Dokter kami tidak melarang kerokan, asal kulitnya tidak sampai terluka.
fix.english: Our doctor doesn't forbid kerokan, as long as the skin doesn't get injured.
fix.grammar: Asal = as long as (condition): asal kulit tidak terluka = as long as the skin isn't hurt.

issue: Word-for-word calque of 'is always in Grandma's bag wherever she goes': existence verb 'ada di dalam tas' cannot take the direction phrase 'ke mana-mana'. Indonesian needs a motion verb to carry 'everywhere'.

fix.target: Balsam hangat ini selalu dibawa nenek ke mana-mana di dalam tasnya.
fix.english: Grandma takes this warming balm everywhere in her bag.

issue: 'Menitip salam' is a hybrid register form: conversational Indonesian says 'titip salam', the full formal form is 'menitipkan salam'. Bare meN- without -kan on titip is the one variant nobody models.

fix.target: Ibu titip salam dan doa untuk tantemu yang sedang sakit.
fix.english: Mom sends her greetings and prayers for your aunt who is sick.
fix.grammar: Titip salam = pass greetings through someone: ibu titip salam = mom sends her regards.

issue: English gloss calques the membuat+passive frame: 'Strong winds made the flight to Lombok get postponed' is not natural English. Indonesian sentence is fine.

fix.english: Strong winds caused the flight to Lombok to be postponed until tomorrow morning.

issue: Tip factual error: glosses the root 'putus' as 'decide'. Putus means broken/severed/cut off; the verb 'decide' is memutuskan. As written the tip teaches a wrong word meaning. Sentence itself is excellent.

fix.grammar: ke-...-an also makes nouns from verbs: memutuskan decide, keputusan decision; sempat manage to, kesempatan chance.

issue: Collocation: friendships 'berawal dari', not 'mulai dari'. 'Persahabatan kami mulai dari kos yang sama' is clipped and off-collocation — mulai dari is the 'starting from/ranging from' frame, not 'originated in'.

fix.target: Persahabatan kami berawal dari kos yang sama lima belas tahun lalu.

issue: Site vocabulary: workers say 'lokasi proyek' (or 'proyek' alone) for a construction site; 'lokasi pembangunan' is planning-document language. Tool/PPE vocab (helm, sarung tangan) is otherwise precise; wajib register fits a safety rule.

fix.target: Helm dan sarung tangan wajib dipakai semua pekerja di lokasi proyek ini.

issue: Set idiom clipped: 'dibahas panjang' — the fixed collocation is 'dibahas panjang lebar' (discussed at length). Bare 'panjang' reads as truncated.

fix.target: Usul yang kamu tulis kemarin dibahas panjang lebar dalam rapat direksi tadi pagi.

issue: Orthography: 'lebaran' lowercase. Lebaran is a proper noun (the holiday) and is capitalized — the deck itself writes 'Lebaran' in its three other occurrences, so this card breaks internal consistency too. Sentence and perantauan tip are otherwise excellent.

fix.target: Setiap Lebaran, rumah kami penuh dengan saudara yang pulang dari perantauan.

issue: Dictionary-example-ese: 'sinyal telepon hilang' — nobody says sinyal telepon; it's 'sinyal HP' or just 'tidak ada sinyal'. The bare-sinyal version is the natural remote-area complaint.

fix.target: Peta kertas tetap berguna kalau tidak ada sinyal di daerah terpencil.
fix.english: A paper map is still useful if there is no signal in a remote area.

issue: Proverb wording off: canonical form is 'Buah jatuh tak jauh dari pohonnya' — the fixed proverb uses 'tak', and normalizing it to 'tidak' breaks the quoted wording (severe under proverb-exactness rule; a learner who repeats the card's version will sound off). 'tak' is already deck vocabulary via id-3930 'Tak kenal maka tak sayang'. Application clause and tip are good.

fix.target: Buah jatuh tak jauh dari pohonnya; anak itu rajin persis seperti ibunya.

issue: English gloss calques 'melahirkan': 'every answer gives birth to a new question' is translationese. Indonesian melahirkan = 'generate/spark' in this frame; the Indonesian sentence itself is natural and vivid.

fix.english: That child's curiosity never runs out; every answer sparks a new question.
